stem: The probability that a sales representative closes a deal on any given client visit is 0.4, independently of other visits. She visits 5 clients in a day. Find the probability that she closes deals on at least 3 clients. [Given: (0.6)^5 = 0.07776, (0.6)^4 = 0.1296, (0.6)^3 = 0.216, (0.6)^2 = 0.36]

per_option_rationale.rationale: 0.68256 = 1 - 0.31744; the student computed P(X<3) instead of P(X>=3) via complement confusion, subtracting from the wrong event.
0.23040 = P(X=3) only; the student found exactly 3 instead of at least 3, missing P(4) and P(5).
0.08704 = P(X=4)+P(X=5) = 0.07680+0.01024; the student started from at least 4 instead of at least 3.

explanation_sections.punchline: At least 3 from 5 requires three Binomial terms; missing any one gives a wrong answer from four offered distractors.
explanation_sections.approach: Model: Binomial(n=5, p=0.4). Identify: at least 3 means k=3,4,5. Compute each term using p^k*q^(n-k) with given hints. Sum the three. Cross-check: complement = P(0)+P(1)+P(2) should equal 1-0.31744=0.68256.
explanation_sections.lesson: For at-least-k problems with small n, enumerate every term above the threshold; never stop at the first term.
explanation_sections.timing: 120 seconds. Three terms; use hints for powers. Trap: choosing only P(X=3)=0.23040 or the complement 0.68256.
